card.name: Early 20th-century history timelines
card.fires_on: Small words and punctuation inside narrative history of the late 1800s to early 1900s, such as Canadian politics, labor unions and new inventions. It fires on the linking word or mark right after a date, a title or an invention.

modes.label: Dated history entries
modes.description: Colon or arrow right after a year or decade in a historical timeline.
modes.example: 1870s<<:>> Alexander Graham Bell invents the telephone.

modes.label: Politics and labor history
modes.description: Linking words after offices, owners or reformers in early 20th-century political and labor stories.

modes.label: Era technology lists
modes.description: Commas and 'and' inside lists of period inventions like telephone and radio.
modes.example: There was even talk of telephones<<,>> radios, television, airplanes and automobiles.

card.writes: It pushes toward railway and steam-age words and away from television and computer words.
card.plain: It marks passages about history from the steam and railway age, and discourages modern media words.
